valueType: species numeric id (FishSpecies.ids; default ids 0-64, remappable via config/mariculture/fish-mappings.cfg)
dominance: species-level: FishSpecies.isDominant(); dominant species allele goes upper; tie -> coin flip (FishDNASpecies.getDominant FishDNASpecies.java:30-51; note tie branch: nextInt(2)==0 puts option2 first)
inheritance: Egg stores 4 values [fatherUpper, fatherLower, motherUpper, motherLower] (FishyHelper.generateEgg, FishyHelper.java:295-302). Child takes allele1 = list[nextInt(2)] (from parent passed first = feeder male slot) and allele2 = list[2 + nextInt(2)] (female) (FishyHelper.java:162-163); attemptMutation is the identity for every gene (FishDNABase.java:53-58, never overridden). If a species mutation fires, the mutated slot(s) are overwritten with the child species defaults (FishyHelper.java:181-192). Finally the two alleles are ordered by dominance: the allele whose value falls in a range flagged dominant becomes upper (expressed) and the other lower; if both or neither are dominant the order is a 50/50 coin flip (FishDNA.getDominant FishDNA.java:81-97 + FishDNABase.swapDominance FishDNABase.java:69-89). A value that falls in no display range keeps dominance=0, i.e. is treated as dominant. Then species mutation: see mutations.json; each matching mutation rolls twice independently (upper, then lower).
tooltipDisplay: not in tooltip lines; drives item name "<Upper>-<Lower> Hybrid" or "<Species>" + gender symbol (ItemFishy.java:76-82)

defaultFromSpecies: random nextInt(2), evaluated independently for upper and lower (FishDNAGender.java:23-25)
dominance: BUG: getDominant computes both dominance values from option1 (FishDNAGender.java:16-17), so it is always a tie -> 50/50 order.

boosterCompounding: getDNA/getLowerDNA return clamp(stored+booster). generateEgg stores the boosted read values (FishyHelper.java:297-300) and makeBredFish re-reads with getDNA and writes back during dominance sorting (FishyHelper.java:199-206), so each bred generation stores parent+2*booster (clamped).
